requirements.quote:
Extensions SHOULD avoid changing protocol elements defined in this
   document or elements for which no extension mechanism is defined.
   This includes changes to the layout of frames, additions or changes
   to the way that frames are composed into HTTP messages (Section 8.1),
   the definition of pseudo-header fields, or changes to any protocol
   element that a compliant endpoint might treat as a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1).
requirements.condition: When defining an extension, especially where this document or no extension mechanism defines the affected protocol element.
requirements.required_behavior: Avoid changing the identified protocol elements, including frame layouts, frame composition into HTTP messages, pseudo-header definitions, and elements that compliant endpoints might treat as connection errors.
requirements.why_checkable: An extension specification and implementation can be inspected for changes to the enumerated existing protocol elements.

requirements.quote:
An extension that changes existing protocol elements or state MUST be
   negotiated before being used.
requirements.condition: When an extension changes an existing protocol element or protocol state.
requirements.required_behavior: Negotiate the extension before using it.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the extension before negotiation completes.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can attempt to use a state- or element-changing extension before and after negotiation and observe whether use is gated.

requirements.quote:
the layout of the HEADERS frame cannot be used until the peer has
   given a positive signal that this is acceptable.
requirements.condition: When an extension changes the layout of the HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Wait for a positive signal from the peer before using the changed layout.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the changed HEADERS layout before the peer positively signals acceptance.
requirements.why_checkable: The transmitted HEADERS layout can be checked before and after the peer's positive signal.

requirements.quote:
flow controlled requires a change in semantics that both endpoints
   need to understand, so this can only be done through negotiation.
requirements.condition: When treating frame types other than DATA as flow controlled.
requirements.required_behavior: Enable the changed flow-control semantics only through negotiation understood by both endpoints.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Unilaterally treating non-DATA frames as flow controlled without negotiation.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify whether non-DATA flow control is activated without a completed bilateral negotiation.

requirements.quote:
a setting is used for extension negotiation, the initial value MUST
   be defined in such a fashion that the extension is initially
   disabled.
requirements.condition: When a setting is used to negotiate an extension.
requirements.required_behavior: Define the setting's initial value so that the extension is initially disabled.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Defining an initial setting value that enables the extension.
requirements.why_checkable: The setting definition and endpoint behavior before receiving a new value can be checked for an initially disabled state.

requirements.quote:
This specification defines a number of frame types, each identified
   by a unique 8-bit type code.
requirements.condition: For each defined frame type.
requirements.required_behavior: Identify the frame type with a unique 8-bit type code.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assigning the same type code to multiple defined frame types or using a type code wider than 8 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame type registries and encoded frame headers can be checked for code width and uniqueness.

requirements.quote:
DATA frames (type=0x00) convey arbitrary, variable-length sequences
   of octets associated with a stream.
requirements.condition: When encoding or processing a DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use frame type 0x00 and associate its variable-length octet sequence with a stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Encoded DATA frames can be inspected for their type code, payload form, and stream association.

requirements.quote:
DATA frames MAY also contain padding.  Padding can be added to DATA
   frames to obscure the size of messages.
requirements.condition: When sending a DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The sender may include padding.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser or sender can be tested with DATA frames both with and without padding.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a DATA frame header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode a 24-bit Length field followed by an 8-bit Type field fixed to 0x00.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Type value other than 0x00 for a DATA frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The field widths, order, and fixed type value are directly observable in serialized frames.

requirements.quote:
Unused Flags (4),
     PADDED Flag (1),
     Unused Flags (2),
     END_STREAM Flag (1),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the DATA frame flags octet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use four unused bits, one PADDED bit, two unused bits, and one END_STREAM bit in the stated order.
requirements.why_checkable: The positions and widths of all bits in the flags octet can be inspected in serialized DATA frames.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Stream Identifier (31),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the stream identifier portion of a DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use one reserved bit followed by a 31-bit Stream Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit widths and ordering can be verified directly from the serialized frame header.

requirements.quote:
[Pad Length (8)],
     Data (..),
     Padding (..2040),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the payload of a DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent an optional 8-bit Pad Length, variable-length Data, and zero to 2040 bits of Padding in that order.
requirements.why_checkable: Payload field presence, ordering, and encoded sizes can be checked against serialized DATA frames.

requirements.quote:
Pad Length:  An 8-bit field containing the length of the frame
      padding in units of octets.  This field is conditional and is only
      present if the PADDED flag is set.
requirements.condition: When a DATA frame carries a Pad Length field.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Pad Length as an 8-bit count of padding octets and include it only when the PADDED flag is set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including the Pad Length field when the PADDED flag is not set.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag, field presence, field width, and relation between the encoded value and padding length are directly testable.

requirements.quote:
Data:  Application data.  The amount of data is the remainder of the
      frame payload after subtracting the length of the other fields
      that are present.
requirements.condition: When determining the Data field length of a DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Compute the Data length as the frame payload length minus the lengths of all other present payload fields.
requirements.why_checkable: Given the payload length and optional fields, the expected Data length can be calculated and compared with parser behavior.

requirements.quote:
Padding:  Padding octets that contain no application semantic value.
      Padding octets MUST be set to zero when sending.
requirements.condition: When sending a DATA frame containing padding octets.
requirements.required_behavior: Set every padding octet to zero and treat padding as having no application semantic value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending a non-zero padding octet or interpreting padding as application data.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized padding values and delivered application data can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
not obligated to verify padding but MAY treat non-zero padding as
      a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a receiver detects non-zero padding in a DATA frame.
requirements.error_behavior: The receiver may treat the condition as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR; it is not required to verify padding.
requirements.why_checkable: Receiver behavior can be observed after supplying a DATA frame with non-zero padding.

requirements.quote:
PADDED (0x08):  When set, the PADDED flag indicates that the Pad
      Length field and any padding that it describes are present.
requirements.condition: When the DATA frame PADDED flag, value 0x08, is set.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Pad Length field and the padding it describes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Setting PADDED while omitting the Pad Length field or its described padding.
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized frame with PADDED set can be checked for the required fields and padding length.

requirements.quote:
END_STREAM (0x01):  When set, the END_STREAM flag indicates that this
      frame is the last that the endpoint will send for the identified
      stream.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends a DATA frame with END_STREAM (0x01) set.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat that frame as the last frame the endpoint will send for the identified stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending another frame for that stream after declaring this frame to be the endpoint's last.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame trace can be checked for transmissions on the identified stream after END_STREAM.

requirements.quote:
stream.  Setting this flag causes the stream to enter one of the
      "half-closed" states or the "closed" state (Section 5.1).
requirements.condition: When END_STREAM is set on a DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream into the applicable half-closed state or the closed state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Leaving the stream in a state that permits the sending endpoint to send further frames on it.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream state immediately after processing or sending END_STREAM can be inspected.

requirements.quote: DATA frames MUST be associated with a stream.
requirements.condition: For every DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the DATA frame with a stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a DATA frame without a stream association.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame's Stream Identifier can be inspected to determine whether it identifies a stream.

requirements.quote:
received whose Stream Identifier field is 0x00, the recipient MUST
   respond with a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a DATA frame is received with Stream Identifier 0x00.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accepting the frame as a valid stream-associated DATA frame.
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A DATA frame with stream identifier zero can be injected and the resulting connection error observed.

requirements.quote:
DATA frames are subject to flow control and can only be sent when a
   stream is in the "open" or "half-closed (remote)" state.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends a DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply flow control and send it only while the stream is in the open or half-closed (remote) state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending a DATA frame in any other stream state or without satisfying flow control.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame transmission can be tested across stream states and available flow-control credit.

requirements.quote:
DATA frame payload is included in flow control, including the Pad
   Length and Padding fields if present.
requirements.condition: When accounting for flow control of a DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Count the entire DATA payload, including any Pad Length and Padding fields, against flow control.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Excluding Pad Length or Padding octets from flow-control accounting.
requirements.why_checkable: Flow-control window consumption can be compared with the full encoded payload length.

requirements.quote:
whose stream is not in the "open" or "half-closed (local)" state, the
   recipient MUST respond with a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type
   STREAM_CLOSED.
requirements.condition: When a DATA frame is received for a stream not in the open or half-closed (local) state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accepting the DATA frame as valid for that stream state.
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a stream error of type STREAM_CLOSED.
requirements.why_checkable: A DATA frame can be supplied in each invalid receive-side stream state and the stream error inspected.

requirements.quote:
The total number of padding octets is determined by the value of the
   Pad Length field.
requirements.condition: When a DATA frame contains a Pad Length field.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Pad Length value as the total number of padding octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a padding length that differs from the Pad Length value.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Pad Length can be compared directly with the number of trailing padding octets.

requirements.quote:
frame payload or greater, the recipient MUST treat this as a
   connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When the padding length is greater than or equal to the DATA frame payload length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accepting the frame as valid.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the condition as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary cases where padding length equals or exceeds payload length can be supplied and the connection error observed.

requirements.quote:
The HEADERS frame (type=0x01) is used to open a stream (Section 5.1),
   and additionally carries a field block fragment.
requirements.condition: When encoding or processing a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use type 0x01, use the frame to open a stream as applicable, and carry a field block fragment.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame type, stream-opening effect, and presence of a field block fragment can be inspected.

requirements.quote: HEADERS frame can carry a header section or a trailer section.
requirements.condition: When interpreting the field block carried by a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow the HEADERS frame to carry either a header section or a trailer section.
requirements.why_checkable: Parser behavior can be tested with HEADERS frames representing initial headers and trailers.

requirements.quote:
HEADERS frames can be sent on a stream in the "idle", "reserved
   (local)", "open", or "half-closed (remote)" state.
requirements.condition: When sending a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Send it only on a stream in the idle, reserved (local), open, or half-closed (remote) state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending a HEADERS frame in a stream state outside the listed set.
requirements.why_checkable: HEADERS transmission can be attempted in every stream state and compared with the enumerated allowed states.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the visible initial fields of a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode a 24-bit Length field followed by an 8-bit Type field fixed to 0x01.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Type value other than 0x01 for a HEADERS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The widths, ordering, and fixed type value are directly observable in the serialized frame header.
